images.title: Times 10 moves every symbol up
images.purpose: Shows that multiplying 121 by 10 turns every symbol into the next landmark, giving 1210.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Before and after: one Egyptian numeral on top, four downward arrows, and the new numeral below.
images.exact_structure: Top row: one coil (flat rope spiral), two heels (upside down U shapes) and one vertical stroke, all in teal (#0072B2), labelled 121 on the left. Exactly 4 dark arrows point straight down, one from each symbol, each labelled × 10. Bottom row, directly under: one lotus flower on a stem under the coil, two coils under the heels and one heel under the stroke, all in amber (#E69F00), labelled 1210 on the left. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: To multiply by 10, move every symbol up one landmark.
images.description: Shows that multiplying 121 by 10 turns every symbol into the next landmark, giving 1210.

image_decisions.why: The rule for multiplying by the base is a symbol by symbol change, which a before and after shows directly.
